findings.summary: H1 fixed: claim-then-refund with refundSettledAt and a grace-gated NOT_FOUND sweeper; late-commit e2e added
M1 fixed: free retry removed (reuse charges 5); an unknown debit on a new file discards the upload
M2 fixed: inline processing from the presigned URL carried in content.generation.requested
M3 fixed: bounded OCR wait (AI_CHAT_DOCUMENT_WAIT_MS, default 120 s) wired at ai-chat.service.ts:675

Live real OCR -> COMPLETED and real ai-service generation not exercised end to end. Environmental, not a code defect: needs a Gemini key and a public R2 host; the private-host SSRF switch is F3, carried to phase 16. Money and data paths around it were proven live with real envelopes, and the real worker's download/refuse path ran live
A user token returns UNAUTHENTICATED (aud check runs first) instead of PERMISSION_DENIED. Still refused, no security impact; accepted deviation recorded in the plan
A debit committing more than REFUND_SWEEP_GRACE_MS (2 min) after its compensating refund would still be missed. Same bound exam accepts; consider a finance-side refund tombstone later
The 1 h presigned URL in content.generation.requested can expire under a long backlog; the job then fails and is refunded
Upload charge uses the client-supplied size (pre-existing)
JWKS refresh has no single-flight guard; a stale cache during an auth outage rejects all calls
A document the caller does not own returns 403, not the repo rule's 404 (same as HEAD)
L7 fixed: PERMISSION_DENIED and INVALID_ARGUMENT are definitive refusals (document and exam)
L2 fixed: creditCharged cleared in the same tx as the failure refund
L6 fixed: completed handler uses its own tx and releases the lock after commit
